chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The Qa'im has two disappearances; one is short and the other is long. In the first disappearance, only the special group of his Shia knows his location, and in the second, only the special group of his guardians in his religion knows his location."

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the awaited Imam Mahdi
key_terms.خَاصَّةُ شِيعَتِهِ: The special/close group of his Shia

ai.seo_question: What are the two stages of the Imam's disappearance (ghayba) according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of the two occultations (al-Ghaybatan), distinguishing between the Minor Occultation (Ghaybat al-Sughra) where the Imam communicated through four specific deputies (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'ah), and the Major Occultation (Ghaybat al-Kubra) where knowledge of his location was restricted to his most devoted guardians before becoming general. This distinction underscores the gradual transition from direct, mediated leadership to a period of waiting (Intizar) where the community relies on the general deputies of the scholars. The hadith highlights the theological significance of divine concealment as a test of faith and a mechanism for preserving the Imam from political elimination.
